answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a refundable stake that is slashed when an identity misbehaves, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then becomes a costly signal: honest work slowly builds standing, while a fresh identity starts at zero and cannot borrow trust. Like crossing a tundra, every step costs energy, and one ridge of verified history separates established agents from disposable clones, because attackers must pay the stake and rebuild reputation for each fake.
